missing_information_behavior: Do not recommend potassium until renal function, medication list, existing supplements and clinical indication have been reviewed.
safety_exclusions: Do not infer potassium deficiency from kidney disease, fatigue or cramps alone.
Do not recommend potassium-based salt substitutes without checking renal and medication context.
Do not advise stopping prescribed medicines.
professional_escalation_conditions: Chronic kidney disease, dialysis, known hyperkalemia, heart failure or use of ACE inhibitors, ARBs or potassium-sparing diuretics.
Weakness, palpitations, syncope or abnormal serum potassium.
population_and_context: People with kidney disease or impaired renal function considering potassium supplementation; impaired potassium excretion may raise risk of hyperkalemia.
dose_constraints: No dose from this rule. Require clinician assessment of serum potassium, renal function, indication and interacting medicines.
certainty_and_limitations: NIH ODS Potassium fact sheet describes potassium balance and medication-related hyperkalemia risks. Individual decisions require laboratory and clinical review.
